finding: 5 of 15 drinking-water samples collected from flood-hit Bidur sources tested positive for E. coli; affected sources were chlorinated.
Bidur Municipality reported insufficient drinking water and was supplying displaced camps by tanker.

District water-supply officials reported that river-adjacent drinking-water projects were damaged and pipes were provided to local governments including Uttargaya to arrange temporary supply from local sources.
direction: Confirms disruption; temporary mitigation in place

finding: Clean-water tankering continued; Red Cross assigned to manage water supply across Nuwakot holding centres; drinking-water-source testing commenced.
direction: Confirms continuing WASH concern with active mitigation

finding: Field reporting stated drinking-water access had become a bigger problem than food in Baireni after taps, pipes and distribution lines were damaged; at least 250 households depending on three systems were affected.
Repairs to the Maheshkhola-Bhattatar-Jintetar deep-boring scheme restored drinking-water service to 180 flood-affected households.

WHO reported crowded temporary shelters, damaged water and sanitation systems, difficult road access and increased communicable-disease risk; water quality was being monitored alongside disease trends.
direction: Supports concern in displacement settings; not municipality-specific

finding: Oxfam assessment combined FGDs, KIIs, holding-centre observation and WASH technical observation; direct access to Uttargaya Wards 1–3 was not possible, so findings for those locations remained provisional.
